A1.definition: A. a. as an abbreviation, for the praenomen Aulus. for Absolvo, on the voting-tablet of a judge; hence C. calls A littera salutaris. for Antiquo on a voting-tablet in the Comitia. a. d. for ante diem. a.v.c. or a. u. …

accensus1.definition: accēnsus ī, m P. of accenseo, an attendant of a magistrate, apparitor, orderly, C., L.: Neroni: Gabinii.—Plur.

accisus1.definition: accīsus adj. impaired, ruined, disordered, overthrown, destroyed: res: robur iuventutis, L.: opes, H.

accitus2.definition: (accītus ūs), m accio, a summons, call; only abl sing.: istius, at his summons: genitoris, V.

adfectus1.definition: adfectus (aff-) adj. P. of adficio, furnished, supplied, endowed, provided, gifted: audaciā, T.: virtutibus. — Praegn., affected, impaired, weakened, infirm: animi, discouraged, L.: gravi morbo: ita adfectus, ut si ad…

adfectus2.definition: adfectus (aff-) ūs, m ad + 2 FAC-, a state, disposition, mood: animi: dubiis adfectibus errare, in vacillating moods, O.: adfectu tacito laetari, rapture, O.—A desire, fondness for: opes atque inopiam pari adfectu con…

adfinis1.definition: ad-fīnis (aff-) e, adj. (abl. īnī, C.; once īne, T.), adjoining, bordering on: fundo: gens Mauris, L.—Fig., related by marriage: Hegio nobis, T.— Hence, subst.

adfinis2.definition: adfīnis is, m and f a connection by marriage: si me alienus adfinem volet, wants to marry into my family, T.: adfinem reppulisti. —Connected with, sharing, accessory to, implicated in: turpitudini: sceleri: illarum re…

aditus2.definition: aditus ūs, m 1 adeo, a going to, drawing near, approach, access: urbī s uno aditu atque adventu captas: temptare aditūs, seek to approach, V.: viri mollīs aditūs novisse, how to approach gently, V.—A privilege of admi…

adsensus2.definition: adsēnsus (ass-) ūs, m adsentio, an agreement, assent, approval, approbation: omnium adsensu iudicare: partīs adsensibus implent, fulfil their duty by assent, O.—An acceptance as real, C.—Poet., an echo: nemorum, V.

adsero1.definition: ad - serō (ass-) —, situs, ere, to plant at, set near: pō pulus adsita Limitibus, H.: adsitae arbores, Ct.

adsero2.definition: ad-serō (ass-) seruī, sertus, ere, to claim, lay claim to, appropriate (poet.): laudes, O.: me caelo, i. e. as of heavenly origin, O.: Iovem sibi patrem, Cu.: virginem in servitutem, as his slave, L.: liberali illam c…

adversum1.definition: adversum (advor-) adv. and praep., see 2 adversus.

adversum2.definition: adversum ī, n the opposite direction: hic ventus adversum tenet Athenis proficiscentibus, N.: in adversum Romani subiere, directly to the hill, L.— Fig., opposed, contrary, hostile, adverse, unfavorable, unpropitious:…

adversum3.definition: adversum ī, n misfortune, calamity, disaster: uti Advorsa eius per te tecta sient, T.: nihil adversi exspectare: si quando adversa vocarent, if misfortune should require, V.

agnatus2.definition: āgnātus (ad-g-) ī, m agnascor, a relation on the father's side, C.—Plur, children born after the father has made his will, Ta.

alienum2.definition: aliēnum ī, n the property of a stranger, another's possessions: alienum appetere: alieni appetens sui profugus, S.: necessitas ex alieno praedandi, L.: exstruere aedificium in alieno: aliis sua eripere, aliis dare ali…

aliquantum1.definition: aliquantum ī, n neut. of aliquantus, a little, some, a considerable amount, something: ex cottidianis sumptibus: auri: itineris, Cs.: muri, L.: equorum et armorum, S.

aliquantum2.definition: aliquantum adv., somewhat, in some degree, considerably, not a little: commotus: illius conatūs reprimere: modum excedere, L.: intellegere.— With comp: ad rem avidior, T.: praeda spe maior, L.

all-.definition: al-l- in words compounded with ad, see adl-.

altum1.definition: altum ī, n altus, height: ordo editus in altum: genitum demisit ab alto, i. e. from heaven, V.—Meton., depth, the deep, the sea: terris iactatus et alto, V.: in altum Vela dabant, V.: urget ab alto Notus, V.: aditus e…

amissus2.definition: āmissus ūs, m amitto, a loss: Siciliae, N.

arbitratus2.definition: (arbitrātus, ūs, m), only abl. arbitror, mediatiou, arbitration: cuius arbitratu de negotiis consuleretur, S.—Will, pleasure, free-will, choice: (sententias) exposui arbitratu meo: suo arbitratu vendere.

arcessitus2.definition: (arcessītus ūs),m arcesso, a calling for, summons; only abl sing.: ipsius arcessitu venire.

armatus1.definition: armātus adj. with sup. P. of armo, armed, equipped, in arms: consuli armatus obstitit: plebes, S.: classes, V.: cohors, Ta.: milia armata quinquagenta, soldiers, Cs.: quasi armatissimi fuerint: facibus, L.: ursi ungui…

armatus2.definition: (armātus ūs), m only abl sing. armo, armor, equipment: haud dispari, L. — Meton., armed men, troops: graviore, L.

assa1.definition: āssa ae, f assus, sc. nutrix, a dry nurse, Iu.

assa2.definition: āssa ōrum, n plur., see assus.

asse-.definition: as-se- in words compounded with ad, see ad-se-.

astu1.definition: astū n indecl., a)/stu, a city, T., C., N.

attactus2.definition: attāctus —, m attingo, a touch, contact (only abl sing.): Volvitur attactu nullo, V., O.

auguratus1.definition: augurātus P. of auguro and of auguror.

auguratus2.definition: augurātus ūs, m auguror, the office of augur: insigne auguratū s: auguratu praeditus, Ta.: scientia auguratūs.—Plur., Ta.

autumnus1.definition: autumnus (not auct-), ī, m AV-, autumn: gravis, Cs.: pomifer, H.: letifer, sickly, Iu.: per autumnos, H.: inaequales, changeable, O.

autumnus2.definition: 'autumnus adj., autumnal, of the autumn: frigus, O.'
